2027-04-05.title: The Annunciation of the Lord (transferred from 25 March)
readings: Look, the virgin shall conceive and bear a son, and shall name him Emmanuel, for God is with us
Here I am, Lord; I come to do your will
See, I have come to do your will, O God
You will conceive in your womb and bear a son
2027-04-05.alt: Solemnity of the Lord, transferred. The Annunciation is normally kept on 25 March, nine months before Christmas. In 2027 that day was Holy Thursday, and no solemnity may be celebrated in Holy Week or in the Octave of Easter; when this happens the Annunciation is moved to the Monday after the Second Sunday of Easter. The readings and Mass of the solemnity replace those of Monday of the Second Week of Easter (Acts 4:23–31; John 3:1–8), and St Vincent Ferrer is not commemorated this year. The Gloria and the Creed are said; at the words of the Creed “and by the Holy Spirit was incarnate of the Virgin Mary, and became man” all genuflect (kneel). Because it falls in Eastertide, the Alleluia is added to the antiphons and the Gospel acclamation. Liturgical colour: white.
2027-04-05.verse: Then Mary said, “Here am I, the servant of the Lord; let it be with me according to your word.”
theo: On the day after the Octave of Easter the Church goes back, as it were, nine months before Christmas, to the little house in Nazareth. This year the feast has waited for us. The Annunciation fell on Holy Thursday, and the Church does not let the joy of the Incarnation compete with the Supper, the Cross and the empty tomb; so she keeps it now, in the white light of Easter. The move is not an accident of the calendar but a lesson. The child announced by Gabriel is the same Lord who died and rose. The flesh he received from the Virgin Mary is the flesh that hung on the cross and walked out of the tomb on the third day. In the first reading King Ahaz, frightened by two enemy kings, refuses the sign that God offers him; it sounds pious, “I will not put the LORD to the test,” but it is really fear dressed up as piety. Isaiah answers: “the Lord himself will give you a sign. Look, the young woman is with child and shall bear a son, and shall name him Immanuel.” The Hebrew word, almah, means a young woman of marriageable age; the ancient Greek translation made by Jewish scholars rendered it parthenos, a virgin, and this is the text St Matthew quotes. The Church, with the whole tradition, reads the promise as fulfilled to the letter in the Virgin of Nazareth, and so the Lectionary proclaims it today: “the virgin shall conceive.” The reading ends with the name itself: “God is with us.”

The Letter to the Hebrews lets us hear what the Son said as he entered the world. It quotes our psalm: “Sacrifices and offerings you have not desired, but a body you have prepared for me… See, God, I have come to do your will.” The Annunciation has two yeses. Before Mary says “Here am I,” the eternal Son has said “See, I have come.” The Father prepares a body for him in the womb of the Virgin, and that body will be offered once for all on the cross: “it is by God's will that we have been sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.” The Incarnation is already turned toward the Passover. That is why this feast sits so naturally in the Easter season: the Son took our flesh in order to offer it, and he offered it in order to raise it up. And every time we kneel at Mass and the priest says “This is my Body,” we are before the same body that began to exist in Mary's womb on this day.

Then the Gospel, which Christians have prayed in the Angelus three times a day for centuries. The angel Gabriel is sent “to a town in Galilee called Nazareth,” a village nobody had heard of, “to a virgin engaged to a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David.” He greets her: “Greetings, favored one! The Lord is with you.” The Greek word, kecharitomene, means one who has been and remains filled with grace; the Church sees here the grace that preserved Mary from all stain of sin from her conception. Mary is troubled and ponders; she does not doubt, she asks: “How can this be, since I am a virgin?” The answer reveals the whole Trinity: the Most High is the Father, the Son of the Most High is the child, and “the Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you.” That word overshadow is the word used for the cloud of God's glory that covered the tent of meeting. Mary becomes the new Ark, the place where God dwells. Gabriel adds a sign, her old relative Elizabeth expecting a child, “for nothing will be impossible with God.” And then the yes on which our salvation hung: “Here am I, the servant of the Lord; let it be with me according to your word.” In that moment, says the Creed, he “was incarnate of the Virgin Mary, and became man.” That is why we kneel today when we say those words. The Easter Church kneels before the beginning of everything she celebrates.
conn: The Universal Norms on the Liturgical Year (no. 60) do not allow a solemnity to be celebrated in Holy Week or the Octave of Easter. When 25 March falls in either, the Annunciation is transferred to the Monday after the Second Sunday of Easter, as in 2027 (25 March was Holy Thursday).

Since the reform of 1969 the Roman calendar names the day “the Annunciation of the Lord.” It celebrates the Incarnation of the Son, and at the same time Mary's willing consent; St Paul VI called it a joint feast of Christ and of the Virgin (Marialis Cultus 6).
25 March stands nine months before 25 December. Some early Christian writers also linked 25 March with the day of the Lord's death, so that conception and Passover belong together.

Isaiah 7:14 has the Hebrew almah, a young woman; the Greek Septuagint, made by Jewish translators before Christ, has parthenos, virgin. Matthew 1:23 quotes the Greek, and the Church confesses that the sign is fulfilled in the virginal conception of Jesus.

Greek kecharitomene, a perfect participle: one who has been graced and remains so. It is the angel's name for Mary, and a scriptural root of the doctrine of the Immaculate Conception (Catechism 490–491).
The same verb as the cloud that rested on the tent of meeting when the glory of the Lord filled it (Exodus 40:35, Greek text). Mary is the new dwelling place of God.
Only on the Annunciation and on Christmas does the Missal direct all to genuflect at the words “and by the Holy Spirit was incarnate of the Virgin Mary, and became man.” On other days we bow.

The Angelus prays the Annunciation every morning, noon and evening. In Eastertide it gives way to the Regina Caeli, which asks the Queen of Heaven to rejoice because the Son she bore has risen. Today the two prayers meet.
altar: The body prepared for the Son in Mary's womb is the body offered on the cross and given to us at this altar. The Church prays: “This is my Body,” and the Word made flesh is truly, really and substantially present, as truly as he was present in Nazareth.
Mary welcomed the Word first in faith and then in her womb. Before Communion we too can say her words: let it be with me according to your word.
outline: Ask: what has God asked of you lately, and what did you answer?
Ahaz refuses a sign; God gives one anyway.
Point 2 · A body you have prepared
The Son's yes before Mary's yes.
Point 3 · Here am I, the servant
Why we kneel at the Creed, and why in Easter.
A young woman alone in a small house, an angel, and the silence before the yes.
“Let it be with me according to your word.”
live: At noon, pray the Regina Caeli slowly; then read Luke 1:26–38 and remember that the risen Lord was once a child in Mary's womb.
At Mass today kneel at “and became man” with your whole heart; at home, teach the children why.
Name one thing God is asking of you that you have postponed, and say yes to it today.
The Word was a hidden child for nine months. Pray today for mothers expecting a child, and help one in a practical way.
fathers: The knot of Eve's disobedience was loosed by the obedience of Mary; what the virgin Eve bound by unbelief, the Virgin Mary untied by faith.
Mary conceived Christ first in her heart by faith before she conceived him in her body. Her motherhood would have profited her nothing had she not first carried him blessedly in her mind.

The angel waits for your answer, O Virgin, and the whole world waits with him, kneeling at your feet: Adam and all his children in exile. Speak the word, receive the Word; say yes, and open the door to the Creator.
magis: The Annunciation: the fullness of time, the Holy Spirit and the conception of the Son.
Mary full of grace; her “Fiat” as the obedience of faith.
The virginal conception of Jesus, a work of God beyond human understanding.
Mary, consenting to the divine Word, became the Mother of Jesus and devoted herself wholly to the person and work of her Son.
At the Annunciation Mary entrusted herself to God completely with the obedience of faith.
saints: Daughter of Israel, of Nazareth in Galilee, engaged to Joseph of the house of David, chosen to be the Mother of God. Her yes at the Annunciation opened the way for the Incarnation of the Son.
6–10 Apr: Easter weekdays of the Second Week. 7 Apr: St John Baptist de la Salle, memorial. 11 Apr: Third Sunday of Easter. St Vincent Ferrer (5 Apr) is not commemorated this year.
2027-04-05.prayer: O God, who willed that your Word should take on the reality of human flesh in the womb of the Virgin Mary, grant, we pray, that we, who confess our Redeemer to be God and man, may merit to become partakers even in his divine nature. Who lives and reigns with you in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, for ever and ever. Amen. Let us also pray: Lord Jesus, Word made flesh, you entered our world through the yes of your Mother and rose from the dead in the same flesh you took from her. Give us her faith, that we may hear your word and keep it, and her courage, that we may say each day: let it be with me according to your word. Holy Mary, Mother of God, rejoice, for your Son has risen. Alleluia. Amen.

quick: The Annunciation is moved to today because 25 March was Holy Thursday.
The Son said to the Father: a body you have prepared for me; see, I have come to do your will.
Mary said: here am I, the servant of the Lord; and the Word became flesh in her womb.
2027-04-05.action: At Mass today kneel at the words “and became man”; at noon pray the Regina Caeli as a family.
2027-04-05.question: What is God asking of me now, and am I answering like Ahaz or like Mary?
catechism: The Annunciation inaugurates the fullness of time.
Mary's yes: the obedience of faith.
The Incarnation: the Son of God assumed a human nature.
kidsaint: Mary was a young girl in a small village. One day the angel Gabriel came and said: God has chosen you to be the mother of his Son. Mary was surprised, but she loved God, so she said: yes, let it happen as you say. And Jesus began to grow inside her. Lesson: when God asks something, we can say yes like Mary.
2027-04-05.special: Solemnity of the Annunciation of the Lord, transferred from 25 March. White vestments, Gloria and Creed; all genuflect at “and became man.” Alleluia is added because it is Eastertide.
term: From the Latin for “becoming flesh”: the mystery that the eternal Son of God took a full human nature, body and soul, in the womb of the Virgin Mary by the power of the Holy Spirit, without ceasing to be God (John 1:14; Catechism 461–463). It began at the Annunciation.

family.explain: God sent the angel Gabriel to a girl called Mary in a small town called Nazareth. The angel said: you will have a baby, and he will be the Son of God, and his name will be Jesus. Mary asked how, and the angel said: the Holy Spirit will do it; nothing is impossible for God. Mary said: I am God's servant; let it be as you say.
family.intention: We pray for all mothers who are expecting a baby, and for every child not yet born.
family.ask: Ask: “What does it mean to say yes to God?” Then pray the Hail Mary together slowly, stopping at each line.

illus: A young mother in a fishing village near Kollam was told in the fifth month that her baby would be born with a serious heart condition. Relatives advised her quietly to end the pregnancy. Each night she sat with her rosary and stopped at the first Joyful Mystery. Later she told her parish priest: I kept hearing one sentence, nothing will be impossible with God, and I said to Mary, I do not know how, but let it be. The child needed two operations and is now in school. She did not choose the easy road; she chose the yes.

pm.open: Holy Spirit, who overshadowed the Virgin Mary, come upon us as we pray. Make us listen as she listened. Alleluia. Amen.
share: Ask a sign of the Lord your God (Isaiah 7:11). Where have I, like Ahaz, refused God's help out of fear?
See, God, I have come to do your will (Hebrews 10:7). How does Jesus' own yes to the Father change the way I pray?
Here am I, the servant of the Lord (Luke 1:38). What yes is God asking of me this Easter?
pm.resp: Here I am, Lord; I come to do your will.
interc: For the Church, that like Mary she may welcome the Word and give Christ to the world.
For expecting mothers, especially those afraid or alone, and for every unborn child.
For young people discerning their vocation, that they may hear the angel's “Do not be afraid.”
For all who find it hard to trust God, that nothing may seem impossible to them with God.
For our group, that we may keep the Word in our hearts and bring him to others.
pm.close: Father, your Word became flesh in the womb of the Virgin Mary. By her prayers make us servants of your will and witnesses of your risen Son. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, today the Church does something unusual. In the middle of the Easter season she takes us back to Nazareth, to a quiet house and a young woman at prayer. The Annunciation fell on Holy Thursday this year, so it was moved to today. And how fitting it is: the child announced by the angel is the Lord who has just risen from the dead.

In the first reading King Ahaz is afraid. God offers him a sign, and he refuses with pious words. But God gives a sign anyway: the virgin shall conceive and bear a son, and shall name him Emmanuel, God is with us (Isaiah 7:14; Matthew 1:23). God does not wait for our perfect faith before he comes near.

The Letter to the Hebrews tells us what the Son said when he came into the world: a body you have prepared for me; see, God, I have come to do your will (Hebrews 10:5, 7). Before Mary said yes, the Son said yes. The body prepared in Mary's womb would one day be offered on the cross for us, and that same body rose on Easter morning.

Then the angel comes to Mary: Greetings, favored one! The Lord is with you. Mary does not run away and does not pretend. She asks an honest question: how can this be? And the angel answers: the Holy Spirit will come upon you; nothing will be impossible with God. Then Mary says the most important yes in history: here am I, the servant of the Lord; let it be with me according to your word (Luke 1:38).

Today, when we say the Creed, we will kneel at the words: and by the Holy Spirit was incarnate of the Virgin Mary, and became man. We kneel because God became small for us. The great God who made the stars became a tiny child, hidden for nine months. And at this altar he becomes small again, hidden in the bread that is his Body.

So let us ask Mary today for her faith. Ahaz said no out of fear; Mary said yes out of love. Whatever God is asking of you this Easter, a forgiveness, a vocation, a child, a sacrifice, say with her: let it be with me according to your word. Holy Mary, rejoice, for your Son has risen. Alleluia. Amen.
kids: Children, a long time ago an angel came to a girl named Mary. He said: God wants you to be the mother of his Son, Jesus. Mary said: yes, I am God's servant. And Jesus began to grow inside her, like every baby grows inside its mother.
Today at Mass, when we say “and became man,” we kneel down to say thank you to Jesus for becoming a baby for us. Let us say yes to God like Mary!

intro: Theme: “Here am I, the servant of the Lord; let it be with me according to your word.”
God is with us, the Son's yes, Mary's yes, and the Word made flesh, celebrated in the light of Easter.

q: Look, the young woman is with child and shall bear a son, and shall name him Immanuel.
“Look, the virgin shall conceive and bear a son, and they shall name him Emmanuel,” which means, “God is with us.”
points.apply: Where fear has made you refuse God's help, ask him today for the sign you need, and accept the one he gives.

points.h: A body you have prepared for me
sub: The Son's yes to the Father.
q: I delight to do your will, O my God; your law is within my heart.
And it is by God's will that we have been sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.
points.apply: Offer your body to God each morning this week: your work, your tiredness, your hands, for him.

q: And Samuel said, “Speak, for your servant is listening.”
Then Mary said, “Here am I, the servant of the Lord; let it be with me according to your word.”
points.apply: Each day this week begin your prayer with Samuel's words, then listen in silence for two minutes.

sub: From Nazareth to the empty tomb.
q: O come, let us worship and bow down, let us kneel before the LORD, our Maker!
And the Word became flesh and lived among us, and we have seen his glory, the glory as of a father's only son, full of grace and truth.
points.apply: At every Sunday Creed, bow deeply at “and became man,” and remember that God became small for you.

concl: God kept his promise to give a sign: the Virgin conceived, and God is with us.
The Son who took flesh from Mary offered it on the cross and raised it at Easter; let us say yes with her.
2027-04-05.resolve: Pray the Regina Caeli every noon until Pentecost, and the Angelus every noon after it.
